name: Hearing Rehabilitation and the Deaf Child

reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Screen newborns; diagnose by 3, intervene by 6 months
GJB2 connexin 26 is commonest genetic deafness cause
Meningitis deafness: urgent implant before cochlear ossification
Implants bypass hair cells electrically for profound loss
reference.pathophysiology: Sound transduction fails from hair cell or conduction defects; electrical stimulation of spiral ganglion neurons restores auditory input during developmental plasticity windows that close progressively without stimulation.
additionalDifferentials: Hearing aid versus implant by hair cell survival and severity
Conductive atresia rehabilitation (bone device) versus sensorineural aid
Congenital CMV versus genetic deafness clues
additionalInvestigations: Newborn OAE and automated ABR screening
Diagnostic ABR and age appropriate audiometry
CT and MRI cochlea and nerve before implantation; genetics and CMV testing
